correctness.rationale: Exact angular decomposition gives a weighted polynomial Gram operator. The exterior-power determinant leading term yields eigenvalue exponent 2j+1 and the two positive determinant quotients. The Legendre determinant quotient is h_j; the derivative-functional quotient is the shifted-Jacobi endpoint Christoffel kernel D. The single largest exponent arises at m=0,j=L, giving the factorial coefficient. Eigenline convergence follows from exterior eigenprojector convergence. The package standard-library checker executed 832 exact-rational consistency checks; finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: Progressively narrow equatorial observation belts are a natural spherical inverse/partial-data problem. The theorem describes the entire spectral information-loss hierarchy at every angular order with exact positive constants and provides the sharp least-observable direction and global conditioning exponent and constant for all fixed degrees. These data govern noise amplification and regularization, and go beyond finite-case numerical eigenvalues or routine symbol substitution.
